lines.en: label nikidate15:
I tap on Niki’s name in my phone and wait for her to answer.
lines.zh: 我在手机上点下 Niki 的名字，等她接听。

lines.en: I know it’s a bit of a long shot trying to get her to hang out this late at night, so I am prepared for the worst.
lines.zh: 我知道这么晚了想约她出来有点勉强，所以我做好了最坏的打算。

lines.en: Just...the “worst” in this case is simply calling someone else and seeing what they’re up to instead.
lines.zh: 只不过……在这种情况下，“最坏”也不过是打个电话给别人，看看她们在忙什么。

lines.en: And, in the event that I am unable to go the rest of the night without the color pink, I’m pretty sure Noriko should be working. And she always accepts my presence.
lines.zh: 万一我今晚真的一刻都离不开粉色，我敢肯定 Noriko 应该在上班。而她一向来者不拒。

lines.en: I guess this scientifically proves which Nakayama likes me more.
lines.zh: 我想这科学地证明了，中山家两姐妹里谁更喜欢我。

lines.en: : Hello. Niki Nakayama’s phone. This is her manager.
lines.zh: : 您好。这里是 Niki Nakayama 的手机。我是她的经纪人。

lines.en: : Weird. I could have sworn I dialed her cell number.
lines.zh: : 奇怪。我明明记得我拨的是她手机号。

lines.en: : You did. Which is why I answered with, “Hello. Niki Nakayama’s phone.”
lines.zh: : 你没拨错。所以我才接起来说：“您好。这里是 Niki Nakayama 的手机。”

lines.en: : You don’t sound like Niki at all.
lines.zh: : 你听起来一点也不像 Niki。

lines.en: : I’m- Are you even paying attention?
lines.zh: : 我——你到底有没有在听啊？

lines.en: : Do you have any idea who I am?
lines.zh: : 你知不知道我是谁？

lines.en: : I believe your name was...[nikitemp]?
lines.zh: : 我想您的名字是……[nikitemp]？

lines.en: : As much as I admire the tenacity in both of you still calling me that months later, can you put her on the line?
lines.zh: : 虽然我很佩服你们两个过了这么多个月还在这么叫我，能让她接电话吗？

lines.en: : I’m afraid Niki is-
lines.zh: : 恐怕 Niki 现在——

lines.en: : Oh. Wait. Hold, please.
lines.zh: : 哦。等等。请稍等。

lines.en: : {i}Niki, you’re supposed to go on in five minutes. What are you doing here?{/i}
lines.zh: : {i}Niki，你五分钟后就该上台了。你在这儿干什么？{/i}

lines.en: : {i}Phone. Now.{/i}
lines.zh: : {i}电话。给我。{/i}

lines.en: I listen as Niki snatches her phone back and sends her manager away.
lines.zh: 我听着 Niki 把手机抢回去，把经纪人打发走。

lines.en: And, in other news, I think I’m higher on Niki’s priority list than her job now.
lines.zh: 另外插播一条新闻：我觉得自己在 Niki 心里的优先级已经排到她的工作前面了。

lines.en: Probably.
lines.zh: 大概吧。

lines.en: Okay, maybe not {i}higher{/i}, but at least-
lines.zh: 好吧，也许没排到{i}前面{/i}，但至少——

lines.en: : Stop calling me at night. I’m famous.
lines.zh: : 别在晚上给我打电话。我可是名人。

lines.en: : Are you? I had no idea.
lines.zh: : 是吗？我可一点都不知道。

lines.en: : Ha ha ha. Very funny.
lines.zh: : 哈哈哈。真好笑。

lines.en: : If you can get to the urban district in five minutes, I’ll let you in for free.
lines.zh: : 如果你能在五分钟内赶到市区，我让你免费进场。

lines.en: : Sure, let me just teleport over there really quick.
lines.zh: : 行啊，我这就瞬移过去。

lines.en: : Cool. Just say you’re there for me and they’ll let you in.
lines.zh: : 好。你就说你是为我来的，他们就会放你进去。

lines.en: : It’s your concert. Literally everyone is there for you.
lines.zh: : 那是你的演唱会。字面意义上的每个人都是为你来的。

lines.en: : Jesus, why are you so difficult?
lines.zh: : 老天，你怎么这么难搞？

lines.en: : I’m not even doing anything this time.
lines.zh: : 这次我可什么都没干。

lines.en: : Hah...listen- I have to go on stage now or thousands of people are going to be disappointed.
lines.zh: : 哈……听着——我现在必须上台了，不然成千上万的人要失望了。

lines.en: : But if you want to make your way over to the urban district {i}after{/i} the concert, we can hang out in my hotel.
lines.zh: : 不过演唱会结束{i}之后{/i}，你要是愿意过来市区，我们可以去我酒店里待会儿。

lines.en: : I’m in the master suite at the...Grand Tsukioka...whatever or something?
lines.zh: : 我住在……Grand Tsukioka……管它什么来着的……总统套房。

lines.en: : I feel as if I’ve heard that name before...
lines.zh: : 我觉得我好像在哪儿听过这名字……

lines.en: : Grats. Bye, now.
lines.zh: : 恭喜。挂了。

lines.en: : Wait.
lines.zh: : 等等。

lines.en: : What? What else could you possibly want?
lines.zh: : 什么？你还能想要什么？

lines.en: : Just wanted to say good luck.
lines.zh: : 只是想说一句祝你好运。

lines.en: : Okay, but what do you {i}really{/i} want?
lines.zh: : 好，那你{i}真正{/i}想要的是什么？

lines.en: : To know if I should bring condoms or-
lines.zh: : 想知道我该不该带套——

lines.en: scene black
Jokes on her. I wasn’t going to bring them anyway.
lines.zh: 她上当了。反正我本来也没打算带。

lines.en: scene nikihotel1
A few hours go by before I make it to the hotel which, as I've finally remembered, is owned by Toriko Tsukioka, a totally real student of mine.
lines.zh: 过了几个小时我才赶到酒店——我总算想起来了，这家酒店是 Toriko Tsukioka 的，一个如假包换、货真价实的学生。

lines.en: Well, I guess it’s owned by her family, technically. But it wouldn’t surprise me if they’d just...give it to her or something if she asked nicely.
lines.zh: 嗯，严格来说应该是她家所有。不过如果她好好开口要，他们直接把酒店给她什么的，我也不会意外。

lines.en: Oh yeah, and Niki is here too.
lines.zh: 哦对，还有 Niki 也在这儿。

lines.en: And...she’s...
lines.zh: 而且她……

lines.en: : ...Is that my shirt?
lines.zh: : ……那是我的衬衫吗？

lines.en: : No. Your shirt had a smaller collar.
lines.zh: : 不是。你的衬衫领子要小一点。

lines.en: : And I’d definitely never borrow it and stretch it out to turn it into a more comfortable pajama top.
lines.zh: : 而且我绝对不会借来穿，还把它撑大、改造成更舒服的睡衣上衣。

lines.en: : After all I’ve done for you...
lines.zh: : 我为你付出了那么多……

lines.en: scene nikihotel2
: Yeah. Thanks so much for all of those years of self-doubt. Appreciate it.
lines.zh: : 是啊。真是太感谢那些年的自我怀疑了。受用不尽。

lines.en: : It made you a better person, didn’t it?
lines.zh: : 那让你变成了更好的人，不是吗？

lines.en: : Even if you’re looking a little...different now.
lines.zh: : 哪怕你现在看起来有点……不一样了。

lines.en: scene nikihotel1
: Different for most people, sure. But this is the me you had the pleasure of looking at for pretty much half of your life.
lines.zh: : 对大多数人来说当然不一样。但这可是你有幸看了大半辈子的那个我。

lines.en: : If anything, I’d think it would be weirder for you to look at the super...showy version.
lines.zh: : 要说起来，我反倒觉得你看那个超级……招摇的版本会更奇怪。

lines.en: : Ahh, so this is the {i}real{/i} Niki Nakayama.
lines.zh: : 啊，所以这才是{i}真正的{/i} Niki Nakayama。

lines.en: scene nikihotel3
: Yup. But if you take any pictures or say anything to anyone, I’ll chop your balls off.
lines.zh: : 没错。不过你要是拍了照、或者跟任何人说了，我就把你的蛋切下来。

lines.en: : Afraid of people finding out you wear glasses?
lines.zh: : 怕别人发现你戴眼镜？

lines.en: : Only losers wear glasses. True story.
lines.zh: : 只有失败者才戴眼镜。真的。

lines.en: : I imagine tonight will be incredibly boring, then.
lines.zh: : 那我猜今晚一定会无聊透顶了。

lines.en: scene nikihotel4
: I’m surprised you even came, to be honest. I could have sworn you’d be all like, “Ugh. Too much effort. I’ll just stay home.”
lines.zh: : 说实话，你居然真的来了，我还挺意外的。我还以为你会说什么“呃。太麻烦了。我就待家里吧。”

lines.en: : It’s the least I can do after, as you so aptly put it, “All those years of self-doubt.”
lines.zh: : 在你那么贴切地称之为“那些年的自我怀疑”之后，这算是我最起码能做的。

lines.en: scene nikihotel5
: Woah. That was a really nice thing to say by your standards. I’m impressed.
lines.zh: : 哇哦。以你的标准来说，这话说得可真贴心。我很感动。

lines.en: : And {i}I’m{/i} impressed by how that shirt manages to stay on you despite being stretched to twice its original size.
lines.zh: : 而{i}我{/i}也很感动，那件衬衫被撑到原来两倍大，居然还挂得住。

lines.en: scene nikihotel6
: Thanks. You know, it actually used to belong to this one guy I would always hook up with back when I was sexually active and less...sexually inactive.
lines.zh: : 谢了。你要知道，它以前其实属于某个我过去经常勾搭的男人——那时候我还性活跃，不像现在这么……性不活跃。

lines.en: : You’re not sexually active unless you’re actually having sex, Niki.
lines.zh: : 不真的做爱就不算性活跃，Niki。

lines.en: scene nikihotel7
: Does hand stuff not count anymore? I remember that was kind of a big deal when we were growing up.
lines.zh: : 用手的那些不算了吗？我记得我们小时候那可是件大事。

lines.en: : Was it? Or were you just a nerd who didn’t understand what all of the cool kids were up to until a few years ago?
lines.zh: : 是吗？还是说你就是个书呆子，直到几年前才搞明白那些酷小孩都在干什么？

lines.en: scene nikihotel8
: Oh, yeah. Like you were one of those cool kids, Mr. I’mgoingtospendeverydayatmyneighbor’shouse.
lines.zh: : 哦，对。好像你就是那些酷小孩之一似的，“我要每天泡在邻居家”先生。

lines.en: : That is an incredibly long last name and sounds nothing like Arakawa.
lines.zh: : 这姓氏也太长了吧，而且听起来跟 Arakawa 一点关系都没有。

lines.en: scene nikihotel7
: Oh, that reminds me. What’s a...Nakayarakawayama?
lines.zh: : 哦，这倒提醒我了。什么是……Nakayarakawayama？

lines.en: : Is that just our last names combined?
lines.zh: : 那不就是我们把姓氏拼在一起吗？

lines.en: : I am...assuming you heard that from Noriko.
lines.zh: : 我……猜你是从 Noriko 那儿听来的。

lines.en: : In between declarations of how she was going to “steal you from me,” yes.
lines.zh: : 就在她一遍遍宣告要“把你从我身边偷走”的间隙里，是的。

lines.en: : Of course, I had to inform her that you are not {i}mine{/i} to begin with.
lines.zh: : 当然，我得告诉她，你从一开始就{i}不属于我{/i}。

lines.en: : And also that I would tell our parents if she even {i}tried{/i} stealing you from me.
lines.zh: : 还得告诉她，只要她敢{i}试着{/i}把你从我身边偷走，我就去告诉爸妈。

lines.en: : But...didn’t you just say-
lines.zh: : 可是……你刚才不是说——

lines.en: : Do you wanna sit? My legs are a little tired on account of that whole “putting on a show for thousands of people” thing.
lines.zh: : 你要不要坐？我腿有点酸，毕竟刚“给几千个人表演”了一场。

lines.en: : An idol in her pajamas, sitting on a bed with a known pervert? What would the news outlets say?
lines.zh: : 一个穿着睡衣的偶像，和一个出了名的变态一起坐在床上？那些媒体会说成什么样？

lines.en: : Probably some stuff about how I’m a whore. And how I’m unfit to be a role model for [young_girls] and shouldn’t show my face in stadiums anymore.
lines.zh: : 大概会说我是个婊子。说我不配当 [young_girls] 的榜样，不该再在体育场里露脸。

lines.en: : Woah.
lines.zh: : 哇哦。

lines.en: : Yeah. The idol industry’s rough. I had to fight off a PR nightmare once for just calling some actor cute.
lines.zh: : 是啊。偶像这行很残酷。我有一次只是说了某个演员可爱，就不得不去摆平一场公关噩梦。

lines.en: : See, this is what you get for looking at someone other than me.
lines.zh: : 瞧，这就是你去看别人不看我的下场。

lines.en: : You’re not even that cute anymore. The only thing you have going for you is your eyes.
lines.zh: : 你都已经没那么可爱了。你唯一拿得出手的就只剩眼睛了。

lines.en: : That’s not the {i}only{/i} thing I have going for me.
lines.zh: : 我拿得出手的可{i}不止{/i}那个。

lines.en: : I’m referring to-
lines.zh: : 我说的是——

lines.en: : I know exactly what you’re referring to. Hand stuff, remember?
lines.zh: : 我完全知道你在说什么。用手的那些，记得吗？

lines.en: : If that whole thing about Tsukumogami is real, the old trash can in my room is going to come back and haunt me for all of the jizz-soaked tissues I tossed into it back in the day.
lines.zh: : 如果付丧神那套是真的，我房间里那个旧垃圾桶总有一天会回来找我算账，为了我当年丢进去的那些沾满精液的纸巾。

lines.en: : Well, this conversation took a turn.
lines.zh: : 嗯，这个话题转变得可以。

lines.en: scene black
Niki turns around and hops onto the bed, moving aside to allow me on as well.
lines.zh: Niki 转过身跳上床，往旁边挪了挪，好让我也上来。

lines.en: It’s a much nicer bed than the one we slept in at the beach, but that sort of thing is to be expected in a high class hotel room paid for by Niki’s agency.
lines.zh: 这张床比我们在海边睡的那张好太多了，不过在 Niki 事务所出钱的高级酒店房间里，这也是意料之中。

lines.en: I imagine she stays in places like this all the time.
lines.zh: 我想她经常住这种地方。

lines.en: I wonder if she ever gets lonely sleeping in rooms like this without the comfort...or {i}dis{/i}comfort of an ex-boyfriend nearby.
lines.zh: 我好奇她一个人睡在这样的房间里，身边没有一个前男友带来的安慰……或者说{i}不{/i}适，会不会觉得孤单。

lines.en: scene nikihotel9
: I still can’t believe you destroyed that shirt.
lines.zh: : 我还是不敢相信你毁了那件衬衫。

lines.en: : I still can’t believe you’re so upset about it.
lines.zh: : 我还是不敢相信你为这个气成这样。

lines.en: : If it will make you feel better, I’ll give you one of my old idol outfits to stretch out and wear around your house.
lines.zh: : 如果这样能让你好受点，我可以给你一套我以前的偶像演出服，让你撑大了在家里穿。

lines.en: : I can’t imagine Ami would be very supportive of that new wardrobe choice.
lines.zh: : 我想 Ami 大概不会太支持这个新着装选择。

lines.en: scene nikihotel10
: Well, then {i}she{/i} can have them.
lines.zh: : 那给{i}她{/i}穿好了。

lines.en: : She just needs to grow a little more first. She’s still kinda tiny for her age.
lines.zh: : 她只是得再长大一点。以她的年纪来说，她还是有点小。

lines.en: : Just don’t say that around her. She’ll cry.
lines.zh: : 这话可别当着她说。她会哭的。

lines.en: : I know, I know. Lots of girls are sensitive about their size.
lines.zh: : 我知道，我知道。很多女孩子对自己的尺寸都很敏感。

lines.en: : She’s adorable, though. And, who knows? Maybe you’ll scar {i}her{/i} into becoming an idol as well?
lines.zh: : 不过她很可爱。而且，谁知道呢？也许你能把{i}她{/i}吓出心理阴影，让她也去当偶像？

lines.en: : Maybe it's not too late for me to become a producer instead of a teacher.
lines.zh: : 也许现在改行当制作人而不是当老师，还不算太晚。

lines.en: scene nikihotel11
: Nah. You wouldn’t like being a part of this industry.
lines.zh: : 不。你不会喜欢这一行的。

lines.en: : Too much...thinking on your feet and...reacting to stuff.
lines.zh: : 太多……临场应变……太多要应付的事。

lines.en: : And, at the end of the day, even on days where you made thousands of people smile...things can still feel a little empty.
lines.zh: : 而且说到底，哪怕在那些你让成千上万的人露出笑容的日子里……心里还是会有几分空。

lines.en: : You can never form meaningful relationships with anyone because you belong to the people.
lines.zh: : 你永远没法跟任何人建立有意义的关系，因为你属于大家。

lines.en: : Ah. So you {i}do{/i} get lonely, then.
lines.zh: : 啊。所以你{i}确实{/i}会觉得孤单。

lines.en: scene nikihotel12
: Hm?
: In hotel rooms.
lines.zh: : 在酒店房间里。

lines.en: : I was wondering how many times you must have sat in one of these by yourself.
lines.zh: : 我刚才在想，你一个人坐在这种房间里，到底有过多少次。

lines.en: : Oh, yeah. All the time.
lines.zh: : 哦，是啊。经常。

lines.en: : It’s definitely lonely, but...not a {i}bad{/i} kind of lonely, you know?
lines.zh: : 确实孤单，不过……不是那种{i}糟糕{/i}的孤单，你知道吗？

lines.en: : I really do like my job. And I like focusing on stuff relating to my job.
lines.zh: : 我是真的喜欢我的工作。也喜欢把心思放在跟工作有关的事上。

lines.en: scene nikihotel13
: It helps...take my mind off of stuff.
lines.zh: : 那能帮我……不去想那些事。

lines.en: : Not that “stuff” is anything {i}bad{/i} anymore.
lines.zh: : 倒不是说“那些事”现在有多{i}糟{/i}。

lines.en: : It’s just...stuff...
lines.zh: : 只是……那些事……

lines.en: : I see...
lines.zh: : 这样啊……

lines.en: : Yeah...
scene nikihotel14
: How about you? Do you ever get lonely?
lines.zh: : 你呢？你会觉得孤单吗？

lines.en: : Probably not when you’re surrounded by a bunch of [teenage]girls, right?
lines.zh: : 身边围着一堆 [teenage]女孩的时候大概不会吧，对吧？

lines.en: : I...guess not? I’m not really sure.
lines.zh: : 我……大概不会？我也不太确定。

lines.en: : Being around them does help me take my mind off “stuff” as well, though.
lines.zh: : 不过跟她们待在一起，确实同样能帮我不去想“那些事”。

lines.en: : And none of them steal my clothes, so it’s already better to hang out with them than it is with you.
lines.zh: : 而且她们没有一个偷我衣服，所以光是这一点，跟她们混就比跟你混强。

lines.en: scene nikihotel15
: Well, gee. If I knew you were going to make such a fuss over it, I would have worn something else.
lines.zh: : 哎呀。我要是早知道你会为这个闹成这样，我就穿别的了。

lines.en: : It’s never too late, Niki.
lines.zh: : 现在换也来得及，Niki。

lines.en: : Wanna trade? I like the way the one you’re wearing now looks.
lines.zh: : 要换吗？我觉得你现在穿的那件看起来不错。

lines.en: : Yeah, probably because you stole the only other one I had and turned it into a pajama tarp.
lines.zh: : 那大概是因为你把我仅有的一件偷走了，还把它改造成了一块睡衣篷布。

lines.en: : You want it back?
lines.zh: : 你想要回去？

lines.en: : That is exactly what I have been saying since you took it. Yes.
lines.zh: : 从你拿走它那天起，我说的一直就是这个。对。

lines.en: scene nikihotel16
: Then...
lines.zh: : 那么……

lines.en: : How about you come and get it?
lines.zh: : 你自己来拿怎么样？

lines.en: scene nikihotel17
: Mm! Mnch...mlem...chu...nch...hah...ahh!
lines.zh: : Mm! Mnch...mlem...chu...nch...hah...ahh!

lines.en: jump nikihotelx
label nikihotelx:
Niki latches onto me and pulls my head toward hers, eliminating any possibility for me to “come and get it” as {i}she’s{/i} the one who came to me.
lines.zh: Niki 一把缠住我，把我的头拉向她，彻底断绝了我“过来拿”的可能——因为是{i}她{/i}自己凑过来的。

lines.en: I knew this was coming the moment we sat down, but I have to say that I’m pleasantly surprised by how passionate she’s being right off the bat.
lines.zh: 从我们坐下的那一刻起我就知道会有这一步，不过我得说，她一上来就这么动情，倒让我惊喜。

lines.en: I guess for her, though, this is akin to making up for lost time.
